text:
Eve: Heads-up: we found two invoices for CloudLark (acct CL-77) in the Apr billing run. One is missing the 'egress_bytes' line and is ~$930 less.
Marco: IDs? I can check send history.
Eve: INF-2024-04-2211 (full, $9,230.00) and INF-2024-04-2211-ALT (partial, $8,300.00). The ALT draft was generated and queued but not paid.
Tina: Good that it wasn't paid. Any chance that draft was emailed?
BillingBot: [alert] invoice-renderer: queued email INF-2024-04-2211-ALT to billing@cloudlark.io (job ir-5227)
Marco: Renderer log shows it picked the latest draft id rather than canonical. Snippet:
```
2024-04-22T11:05:02Z INFO renderer.fetch invoice_id=INF-2024-04-2211-ALT status=draft
2024-04-22T11:05:03Z INFO renderer.send_email to=billing@cloudlark.io
```
Eve: Root cause looks like a transient gap: egress usage ingestion lagged by ~3 minutes so the transform in retry path skipped egress.
Tina: Remediation: 1) void the ALT draft and mark 'do not send', 2) re-render canonical PDF and send to billing, 3) add a short wait for cache-rehydration on retries.
Marco: Filed FIN-6274. Attached logs and both PDFs. PR to add wait queued: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/invoice-generator/pulls/1935
BillingBot: [info] FIN-6274 created by Marco assigned to Tina. SLA: 2 business days.
Eve: Also set a short alert to scan for other invoices with '-ALT' or '-ALT' like suffixes in April. Marco, can you run an ES query and post results to FIN-6274?
Marco: Will do. Quick note: this is a good candidate for a small telemetry tag on drafts created from retry paths. Added to the ticket.
Tina: I'll prepare a customer note template: "We noticed an internal duplicate draft that omitted one usage line. You were billed correctly; please see attached corrected invoice." Keep it short.
Eve: Thanks team. I'll hold outbound PDF sends for CL-77 until FIN-6274 is resolved.
